title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第二十九 袁彖 孔稚珪 劉繪
title.en: Volume 48 Biographies 29: Yuan Tuan, Kong Zhigui, Liu Hui
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第二十九 袁彖 孔稚珪 劉繪 Volume 48 Biographies 29: Yuan Tuan, Kong Zhigui, Liu Hui

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷卷四十八‧列傳第二十九

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 48, Biographies 29
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 48, Biographies 29

sentences.zh: 袁彖字偉才，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Tuan, style name Weicai, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tuan, whose style name was Weicai, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖洵，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun was Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun had served as Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父覬，武陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Grand Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui had been Grand Administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 彖少有風氣，好屬文及玄言。

translations.literal: Tuan from youth had a spirited bearing and loved composing literary works and discourses on profound truths.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth Tuan had a spirited temperament and loved literary composition and discourse on the abstruse.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，歷諸王府參軍，不就。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a provincial graduate; he successively received appointments as military aide in various princes' establishments but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a provincial graduate, he was repeatedly offered posts as aide in various princes' households but declined them all.

sentences.zh: 覬臨終與兄顗書曰：「史公才識可嘉，足懋先基矣。

translations.literal: On his deathbed Gui wrote to his elder brother Yan: "The Historian Lord's talent and insight are admirable; he is fully sufficient to honor our ancestral foundation.
translations.idiomatic: As Gui lay dying he wrote to his elder brother Yan: "The Historian Lord's talent and insight are admirable—he is fully equal to carrying on our ancestral foundation.

sentences.zh: 」史公，彖之小字也。

translations.literal: " "Historian Lord" was Tuan's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " "Historian Lord" was Tuan's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 服未闋，顗在雍州起事見誅，宋明帝投顗尸江中，不聽歛葬。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period had ended, Yan rose in revolt in Yong Province and was executed; Emperor Ming of Song cast Yan's corpse into the Yangtze and forbade its retrieval for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mourning obligations were fulfilled, Yan launched a rebellion in Yong Province and was put to death; Emperor Ming of Song threw Yan's body into the Yangtze and forbade anyone to recover it for burial.

sentences.zh: 彖與舊奴一人，微服潛行求尸，四十餘日乃得，密瘞石頭後崗，身自負土。

translations.literal: Tuan, with one old bondservant, went about in commoner's dress and in secret sought the corpse; only after more than forty days did he find it, and he secretly buried it on the hill behind Stone Fortress, personally carrying the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan took one old family slave, dressed as a commoner, and stole about in secret searching for the body; only after more than forty days did he find it, and he secretly buried it on the ridge behind Stone Fortress, carrying the earth on his own back.

sentences.zh: 懷其文集，未嘗離身。

translations.literal: He kept Yan's collected writings and never let them leave his person.
translations.idiomatic: He carried Yan's collected writings with him and never let them out of his hands.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩後，乃改葬顗。

translations.literal: After Emperor Ming died, he had Yan reburied.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Emperor Ming's death did he give Yan a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 從叔司徒粲、外舅征西將軍蔡興宗竝器之。

translations.literal: His uncle by marriage, Minister Over the Masses Can, and his maternal uncle, General Who Pacifies the West Cai Xingzong, both held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle by marriage, Minister Over the Masses Can, and his maternal uncle, General Who Pacifies the West Cai Xingzong, both valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 除安成王征虜參軍，主簿，尚書殿中郎，出爲廬陵內史，豫州治中，太祖太傅相國主簿，祕書丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Aide to the Prince of Ancheng as Pacifier of Barbarians, Recorder, Attendant in the Palace Secretariat, then sent out as Interior Governor of Luling, Administrator of Yuzhou, Recorder to the Founding Emperor as Grand Tutor and Chancellor of State, and Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military aide to the Prince of Ancheng on the Pacification campaign staff, then recorder, palace secretariat attendant, and sent out as interior governor of Luling and Yuzhou administrator; he later served as recorder to the Founding Emperor in his capacities as grand tutor and chancellor of state, and as secretary director.

sentences.zh: 議駮國史，檀超以《天文志》紀緯序位度，《五行志》載當時祥沴，二篇所記，事用相懸，日蝕爲災，宜居《五行》。

translations.literal: He debated the national history: Tan Chao in the 《Astronomical Treatise》 recorded the ordering of celestial coordinates and degrees, while in the 《Treatise on the Five Phases》 he recorded contemporary portents and disasters—the subjects recorded in the two chapters overlapped in substance; solar eclipses as calamities properly belong under the 《Five Phases》.
translations.idiomatic: In debate over the national history he objected that Tan Chao's 《Astronomical Treatise》 recorded the ordering of coordinates and degrees while his 《Treatise on the Five Phases》 recorded contemporary omens and disasters—the two chapters covered overlapping material, and since solar eclipses are calamities they ought to fall under the 《Five Phases》.

sentences.zh: 超欲立處士傳。

translations.literal: Chao wished to establish a "Biographies of Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Chao also wanted to create a separate "Biographies of Recluses."

sentences.zh: 彖曰：「夫事關業用，方得列其名行。

translations.literal: Tuan said: "Only when affairs touch upon public service may one record a person's name and conduct in full.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan said: "Only when someone's affairs bear on public service may one set down his name and conduct at length.

sentences.zh: 今栖遁之士，排斥皇王，陵轢將相，此偏介之行，不可長風移俗，故遷書未傳，班史莫編。

translations.literal: Those who dwell in seclusion today reject the imperial house and look down on generals and ministers—this is an eccentric course of conduct; it cannot be made a model to shift custom by, hence the Records of the Historian did not transmit such lives, and the History of Han did not compile them.
translations.idiomatic: The recluses of today reject the throne and trample on generals and ministers—such eccentric conduct cannot be held up to reshape custom, which is why Sima Qian's history did not pass their lives down and Ban Gu's did not compile them.

sentences.zh: 一介之善，無緣頓略，宜列其姓業，附出他篇。」

translations.literal: A single act of goodness has no warrant for summary omission; one should list their surname and calling and append it within some other section."
translations.idiomatic: A modest virtue cannot simply be dropped; list their surname and profession and attach it as a note in some other chapter."

sentences.zh: 遷始興王友，固辭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Friend of the Prince of Shixing but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Friend of the Prince of Shixing but firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 太祖使吏部尚書何戢宣旨令就。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent Minister of Personnel He Zhan to deliver an edict ordering him to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor dispatched Minister of Personnel He Zhan with an edict commanding him to take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，兼太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat and concurrently served as Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat attendant and concurrently served as vice director in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 又以中書兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He also held the secretariat post while concurrently serving as Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He also retained his secretariat post while serving concurrently as imperial censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 轉黃門郎，兼中丞如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, retaining his concurrent post as censor-in-chief as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman at the yellow gates while continuing to hold the censor-in-chief post as before.

sentences.zh: 坐彈謝超宗簡奏依違，免官。

translations.literal: Because in impeaching Xie Chaozong his memorial was evasive and inconsistent, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office because his impeachment memorial against Xie Chaozong had been equivocal and inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 尋補安西諮議、南平內史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was reappointed Adviser of the Pacification of the West and Interior Governor of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed adviser on the Pacification of the West staff and interior governor of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 除黃門，未拜，仍轉長史、南郡內史，行荊州事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates but had not yet received the investiture when he was transferred to Chief Clerk and Interior Governor of Nan Commandery, acting on Jingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman at the yellow gates but had not yet assumed the post when he was transferred to chief clerk and interior governor of Nan commandery, with charge of Jingzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 還爲太子中庶子，本州大中正。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and as Senior Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as vice director in the heir apparent's household and senior rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 出爲冠軍將軍、監吳興郡事。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might, supervising affairs of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might with supervisory authority over Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 彖性剛，嘗以微言忤世祖，又與王晏不協。

translations.literal: Tuan's nature was stubborn; he once gave offense to the Emperor through a subtle remark, and he was also at odds with Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan was by nature inflexible; he had once offended the Emperor with an oblique remark, and he was also on bad terms with Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 世祖在便殿，用金柄刀子治瓜，晏在側曰：「外間有金刀之言，恐不宜用此物。

translations.literal: The Emperor was in the side hall, using a gold-handled knife to cut a melon, when Yan at his side said: "There is talk abroad of a 'golden knife'; I fear Your Majesty ought not use this object.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was in a side hall, cutting a melon with a gold-handled knife, when Yan beside him said: "There is talk abroad of a 'golden knife'—I fear it would be unwise to use such an object.

sentences.zh: 」世祖愕然，窮問所以。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was startled and pressed to know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was taken aback and pressed to know why.

sentences.zh: 晏曰：「袁彖爲臣說之。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Yuan Tuan told this to your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Yuan Tuan told me this.

sentences.zh: 」上銜怒良久，彖到郡，坐逆用祿錢，免官付東冶。

translations.literal: " The sovereign harbored anger for a long time; when Tuan reached his commandery he was charged with improper use of salary funds, dismissed from office, and sent to the Eastern Workshop prison.
translations.idiomatic: " The sovereign nursed his anger for a long while; when Tuan reached his commandery he was charged with misappropriating salary funds, stripped of office, and consigned to the Eastern Workshop prison.

sentences.zh: 世祖遊孫陵，望東冶，曰：「中有一好貴囚。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Sun Mound and, gazing toward the Eastern Workshop, said: "Among them is one fine and noble prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: On an excursion to Sun Mound the Emperor looked toward the Eastern Workshop and said: "There is a fine gentleman among the prisoners there.

sentences.zh: 」數日，車駕與朝臣幸冶，履行庫藏，因宴飲，賜囚徒酒肉，敕見彖與語，明日釋之。

translations.literal: " Several days later the imperial carriage, with court ministers, visited the workshop, inspected the storehouses, and thereupon feasted; wine and meat were bestowed on the prisoners, and he ordered Tuan brought before him to converse; the next day he was released.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later the imperial procession, with the court ministers, visited the workshop, toured the storehouses, and held a feast there, bestowing wine and meat on the prisoners; he ordered Tuan brought out to speak with him, and released him the following day.

sentences.zh: 尋白衣行南徐州事，司徒諮議，衞軍長史，遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served the affairs of South Xuzhou in plain dress, then Adviser to the Minister Over the Masses, Chief Clerk of the Guards Army, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was handling South Xuzhou affairs in unofficial dress, then served as adviser to the minister over the masses and chief clerk on the guards army staff, and was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 彖形體充腴，有異於衆。

translations.literal: Tuan's physique was full and stout, unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan was corpulent in build, markedly unlike others.

sentences.zh: 每從車駕射雉在郊野，數人推扶，乃能徒步。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed the imperial carriage to shoot pheasants in the countryside, several men had to support and steady him before he could walk on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he accompanied the imperial hunt for pheasants in the open country, several men had to prop him up before he could walk at all.

sentences.zh: 幼而母卒，養於伯母王氏，事之如親。

translations.literal: His mother died when he was young; he was raised by his father's elder brother's wife, Lady Wang, and served her as he would a parent.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was still a boy; he was raised by his aunt, Lady Wang, and treated her exactly as he would his own mother.

sentences.zh: 閨門中甚有孝義。

translations.literal: Within his household he was greatly noted for filial devotion and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Within the family he was renowned for filial devotion and moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Longchang reign.

sentences.zh: 年四十八。

translations.literal: He was forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 諡靖子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Lord Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Lord Jing.

sentences.zh: 孔稚珪

translations.literal: Kong Zhigui
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui

sentences.zh: 孔稚珪字德璋，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Zhigui, style name Dezhang, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui, whose style name was Dezhang, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖道隆，位侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daolong held the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daolong had served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 父靈產，泰始中，罷晉安太守。

translations.literal: His father Lingchan, during the Taishi era, left office as Grand Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingchan had retired from the post of grand administrator of Jin'an during the Taishi era.

sentences.zh: 有隱遁之懷，於禹井山立館，事道精篤，吉日於靜屋四向朝拜，涕泗滂遝。

translations.literal: He harbored a wish for reclusion; on Mount Yujing he established a lodge, practiced the Way with deep devotion, and on auspicious days in a quiet chamber bowed in worship toward the four directions, his tears streaming down in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished thoughts of withdrawal from the world; on Mount Yujing he built a lodge and practiced the Way with fervent devotion, and on auspicious days in a quiet chamber he bowed toward the four directions until tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 東出過錢塘北郭，輙於舟中遙拜杜子恭墓，自此至都，東向坐，不敢背側。

translations.literal: When traveling east he passed the north suburb of Qiantang and always from his boat bowed toward the tomb of Du Zigong; from that point until he reached the capital he sat facing east and dared not turn his back or side to it.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled east and passed the north suburb of Qiantang he would bow from his boat toward the tomb of Du Zigong; from that point until he reached the capital he always sat facing east and never turned his back or even sideways.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，爲中散、太中大夫。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhui era he served as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhui era he held the posts of regular attendant and grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 頗解星文，好術數。

translations.literal: He was well versed in astral lore and fond of numerology and divination.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in astronomy and fond of occult calculation.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，沈攸之起兵，靈產密白太祖曰：「攸之兵衆雖彊，以天時冥數而觀，無能爲也。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was assisting in government, Shen Youzhi raised troops; Lingchan secretly reported to the Founding Emperor: "Though Youzhi's forces are strong, viewed in light of heaven's seasons and the hidden numbers, he can accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was regent, Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Lingchan secretly told him: "Though Youzhi's troops are numerous, judged by the seasons of heaven and the hidden reckonings of fate, he can accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 」太祖驗其言，擢遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor verified his words and promoted him to Grand Master for the Glorious.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founding Emperor found his prediction borne out and promoted him to grand master for the glorious.

sentences.zh: 以簏盛靈產上靈臺，令其占候。

translations.literal: He had Lingchan carried in a bamboo hamper up to the Observatory and ordered him to observe and prognosticate.
translations.idiomatic: He had Lingchan carried in a hamper up to the Observatory and ordered him to observe the heavens and report omens.

sentences.zh: 餉靈產白羽扇、素隱几。

translations.literal: He presented Lingchan with a white-feather fan and a plain reclining armrest.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lingchan a white-feather fan and a plain armrest for reclining.

sentences.zh: 曰：「君性好古，故遺君古物。」

translations.literal: He said: "Sir, you love antiquity, so I leave you these antique objects."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "You love antiquity, so I give you these antique things."

sentences.zh: 稚珪少學涉，有美譽。

translations.literal: Zhigui from youth was broadly learned and enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigui was widely read from his youth and enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 太守王僧虔見而重之，引爲主簿。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Sengqian saw him and valued him, taking him on as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Wang Sengqian took notice of him and valued him, appointing him recorder.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province recommended him as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: The province recommended him as a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 解褐宋安成王車騎法曹行參軍，轉尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the commoner's garb he became Acting Aide in the Law Section on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng as Cavalry General, then was transferred to Attendant in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he served as acting aide in the law section on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng as cavalry general, then was transferred to palace secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲驃騎，以稚珪有文翰，取爲記室參軍，與江淹對掌辭筆。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was Rapid Cavalry General, because Zhigui had literary talent he was taken on as Recorder in the Headquarters and shared charge of drafting with Jiang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor held the post of rapid cavalry general, he recruited Zhigui for his literary gifts as headquarters recorder, pairing him with Jiang Yan to share responsibility for official prose.

sentences.zh: 遷正員郎，中書郎，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Attendant of the Secretariat, and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular attendant, secretariat attendant, and left assistant director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父憂去官，與兄仲智還居父山舍。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he left office and, with his elder brother Zhongzhi, returned to dwell at their father's mountain lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left office and returned with his elder brother Zhongzhi to live at their father's mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 仲智妾李氏驕妒無禮，稚珪白太守王敬則殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi's concubine Lady Li was arrogant, jealous, and without propriety; Zhigui reported her to Grand Administrator Wang Jingze, who had her executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi's concubine Lady Li was arrogant, jealous, and insolent; Zhigui reported her to Grand Administrator Wang Jingze, who had her put to death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，爲司徒從事中郎，州治中，別駕，從事史，本郡中正。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served as Attendant of the Minister Over the Masses, Administrator of the province, Vice Director, Aide, and Senior Rectifier of his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as attendant of the minister over the masses, provincial administrator, vice director, aide, and senior rectifier of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，轉驍騎將軍，復領左丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was transferred to Valiant Cavalry General and again headed the left assistant directorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongming he was transferred to valiant cavalry general and again took charge as left assistant director.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎，左丞如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, retaining the left assistant directorship as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman at the yellow gates while continuing as left assistant director as before.

sentences.zh: 轉太子中庶子，廷尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and Commandant of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director in the heir apparent's household and commandant of punishments.

sentences.zh: 江左相承用晉世張杜律二十卷，世祖留心法令，數訊囚徒，詔獄官詳正舊注。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze had successively used the Jin-era Zhang-Du Code in twenty scrolls; the Emperor paid close attention to statutes and frequently examined prisoners, ordering prison officials to collate and correct the old commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze had long followed the Jin-era Zhang-Du code in twenty scrolls; the Emperor took a close interest in law, frequently interrogated prisoners himself, and ordered the prison officials to revise the old commentaries in detail.

sentences.zh: 先是七年，尚書刪定郎王植撰定律章表奏之，曰：「臣尋《晉律》，文簡辭約，旨通大綱，事之所質，取斷難釋。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the seventh year, Wang Zhi, Editing and Fixing Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat, drafted the statutes and memorialized them, saying: "Your servant has examined the 《Jin Code》: its text is concise and its language spare, its purport grasping the great outline, yet on the matters at issue judgment is hard to extract and explain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the seventh year, Wang Zhi, editing and fixing attendant of the imperial secretariat, drafted the statutes and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has examined the 《Jin Code》: its text is spare and its language concise, its purport grasping the great outline, yet on the matters at issue judgments are hard to extract and apply.

sentences.zh: 張斐杜預同注一章，而生殺永殊。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei and Du Yu comment on the same article, yet life and death are forever at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei and Du Yu comment on the same article, yet their rulings on life and death forever diverge.

sentences.zh: 自晉泰始以來，唯斟酌參用。

translations.literal: From the Jin Taishi era onward, officials have only weighed and drawn on them selectively.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin Taishi era officials have only weighed and applied them selectively.

sentences.zh: 是則吏挾威福之勢，民懷不對之怨，所以溫舒獻辭於失政，絳侯慷慨而興歎。

translations.literal: Thus clerks wield the power of authority and favor, while the people harbor grievances of unanswered justice—hence Wen Shu offered his remonstrance against misgovernment, and the Marquis of Jiang rose up sighing in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus clerks wield arbitrary power while the people nurse grievances of unanswered justice—hence Wen Shu offered his remonstrance against misrule, and the Marquis of Jiang sighed aloud in indignation.

sentences.zh: 皇運革祚，道冠前王，陛下紹興，光開帝業。

translations.literal: The imperial fortune has changed its mandate; Your Majesty's Way surpasses the kings of old; Your Majesty has succeeded and revived, brilliantly opening the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has changed the mandate; Your Majesty's Way surpasses the kings of old; Your Majesty has succeeded and revived, brilliantly opening the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 下車之痛，每惻上仁，滿堂之悲，有矜聖思。

translations.literal: The pain of those just come to office moves Your Majesty's benevolence at every turn; the sorrow filling the hall stirs Your Majesty's compassionate thought.
translations.idiomatic: The suffering of those newly in office touches Your Majesty's benevolence at every turn; the sorrow filling the hall awakens Your Majesty's compassionate concern.

sentences.zh: 爰發德音，刪正刑律，敕臣集定張杜二注。

translations.literal: Thereupon Your Majesty issued a virtuous edict to revise and correct the penal statutes, ordering your servant to assemble and fix the two commentaries of Zhang and Du.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Your Majesty issued a benevolent edict to revise the penal statutes and ordered your servant to assemble and fix the Zhang and Du commentaries.

sentences.zh: 謹礪愚蒙，盡思詳撰，削其煩害，錄其允衷。

translations.literal: Your servant has diligently sharpened his dull wit, exhausting thought in detailed compilation, cutting away what is cumbersome and harmful and recording what is fair and fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has diligently applied his dull wit, exhausting thought in detailed compilation, cutting away what is cumbersome and harmful and recording what is fair and fitting.

sentences.zh: 取張注七百三十一條，杜注七百九十一條。

translations.literal: From Zhang's commentary he took seven hundred thirty-one articles; from Du's, seven hundred ninety-one.
translations.idiomatic: He took seven hundred thirty-one articles from Zhang's commentary and seven hundred ninety-one from Du's.

sentences.zh: 或二家兩釋，於義乃備者，又取一百七條。

translations.literal: Where both schools offered paired explanations that together made the meaning complete, he took another one hundred seven articles.
translations.idiomatic: Where both schools offered paired explanations that together made the meaning complete, he took another one hundred seven articles.

sentences.zh: 其注相同者，取一百三條。

translations.literal: Where the commentaries agreed, he took one hundred three articles.
translations.idiomatic: Where the commentaries agreed, he took one hundred three articles.

sentences.zh: 集爲一書。

translations.literal: He assembled them into one book.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled them into a single work.

sentences.zh: 凡一千五百三十二條，爲二十卷。

translations.literal: In all there were one thousand five hundred thirty-two articles, in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were one thousand five hundred thirty-two articles in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 請付外詳校，擿其違謬。

translations.literal: I request that it be sent out for detailed collation and that errors and inconsistencies be picked out.
translations.idiomatic: I request that it be sent out for detailed collation so that errors and inconsistencies may be identified.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿八座參議，考正舊注。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministers and the eight chief offices joined in deliberation to examine and correct the old commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ministers and the eight chief offices deliberated together to examine and correct the old commentaries.

sentences.zh: 有輕重處，竟陵王子良下意，多使從輕。

translations.literal: Where questions of severity arose, the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, issued instructions that generally favored the lighter penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Where questions of severity arose, the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, issued instructions that generally favored the lighter penalty.

sentences.zh: 其中朝議不能斷者，制旨平決。

translations.literal: Among these, points on which court debate could not decide were settled by imperial rescript.
translations.idiomatic: Points on which court debate could not reach a decision were settled by imperial rescript.

sentences.zh: 至九年，稚珪上表曰：

translations.literal: By the ninth year Zhigui submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year Zhigui submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞匠萬物者以繩墨爲正，馭大國者以法理爲本。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that he who crafts the ten thousand things takes the inked line as his standard, and he who governs a great state takes law and principle as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the craftsman of the ten thousand things takes the inked line as his standard, and the ruler of a great state takes law and principle as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 是以古之聖王，臨朝思理，遠防邪萌，深杜姦漸，莫不資法理以成化，明刑賞以樹功者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity, when they faced the court, pondered good order; they guarded far off against the sprouting of evil and deeply blocked the gradual advance of treachery—all relying on law and principle to accomplish transformation and clarifying punishments and rewards to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the sage kings of antiquity, when they held court, pondered good order; they guarded far off against the sprouting of evil and deeply blocked the gradual advance of treachery—all relying on law and principle to accomplish transformation and clarifying punishments and rewards to establish merit.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下躡曆登皇，乘圖踐帝，天地更築，日月再張，五禮裂而復縫，六樂穨而爰緝。

translations.literal: Bowingly considering that Your Majesty has trodden the calendar and ascended the throne, mounted the chart and trodden the imperial path—heaven and earth rebuilt, sun and moon unfurled anew, the five rites torn apart and sewn together again, the six music scores scattered and now gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: Bowingly considering that Your Majesty has ascended the throne in accordance with the calendar, mounted the imperial chart and taken up the imperial path—heaven and earth have been rebuilt, sun and moon unfurled anew, the five rites torn apart and sewn together again, the six music scores scattered and now gathered in.

sentences.zh: 乃發德音，下明詔，降恤刑之文，申慎罰之典，敕臣與公卿八座共刪注律。

translations.literal: Thereupon Your Majesty issued a virtuous pronouncement and sent down a luminous edict, promulgating texts of compassionate punishment and reaffirming the canon of cautious penalties, ordering your servant together with the ministers and eight chief offices jointly to revise the annotated statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Your Majesty issued a benevolent pronouncement and sent down a luminous edict, promulgating texts of compassionate punishment and reaffirming the canon of cautious penalties, ordering your servant together with the ministers and eight chief offices jointly to revise the annotated statutes.

sentences.zh: 謹奉聖旨，諮審司徒臣子良，稟受成規，創立條緒。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully received the sacred command, consulted and examined with the Minister Over the Masses, your servant Zi Liang, received the established regulations, and set up the framework of articles.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully received the sacred command, consulted with the Minister Over the Masses, your servant Zi Liang, received the established regulations, and set up the framework of articles.

sentences.zh: 使兼監臣宋躬、兼平臣王植等抄撰同異，定其去取。

translations.literal: He assigned the Concurrent Supervisor, your servant Song Gong, and the Concurrent Adjudicator, your servant Wang Zhi, and others to copy and compile similarities and differences and determine what to retain and what to discard.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned the concurrent supervisor, your servant Song Gong, and the concurrent adjudicator, your servant Wang Zhi, and others to copy and compile similarities and differences and determine what to retain and what to discard.

sentences.zh: 詳議八座，裁正大司馬臣嶷。

translations.literal: The eight chief offices deliberated in detail; the Grand Marshal, your servant Yan, passed final judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The eight chief offices deliberated in detail; the grand marshal, your servant Yan, passed final judgment.

sentences.zh: 其中洪疑大議，衆論相背者，聖照玄覽，斷自天筆。

translations.literal: Among these, great doubts and major debates on which the multitude of opinions conflicted were settled by Your Majesty's sage illumination and mysterious scrutiny, decided by the brush of heaven itself.
translations.idiomatic: Among these, great doubts and major debates on which opinions conflicted were settled by Your Majesty's sage illumination, decided by the brush of heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 始就成立《律文》二十卷，《錄敘》一卷，凡二十一卷。

translations.literal: At last the 《Statutory Text》 in twenty scrolls and the 《Record and Preface》 in one scroll were completed—in all twenty-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: At last the 《Statutory Text》 in twenty scrolls and the 《Record and Preface》 in one scroll were completed—in all twenty-one scrolls.

sentences.zh: 今以奏聞，請付外施用，宣下四海。

translations.literal: I now submit this for Your Majesty's information and request that it be sent out for application and proclaimed throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I now submit this for Your Majesty's information and request that it be sent out for application and proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞老子、仲尼曰：「古之聽獄者，求所以生之；

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that Laozi and Zhongni said: "Those who heard cases in antiquity sought means to let men live;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that Laozi and Confucius said: "Those who heard cases in antiquity sought means to let men live;

sentences.zh: 今之聽獄者，求所以殺之。

translations.literal: those who hear cases today seek means to put men to death."
translations.idiomatic: those who hear cases today seek means to put men to death."

sentences.zh: 」「與其殺不辜，寧失有罪。

translations.literal: " "Rather than execute the innocent, better to let the guilty go free.
translations.idiomatic: " "Better to let the guilty go free than to execute the innocent.

sentences.zh: 」是則斷獄之職，自古所難矣。

translations.literal: " Thus the duty of judging cases has been difficult since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the duty of judging cases has been difficult since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今律文雖定，必須用之；

translations.literal: Now though the statutory text is fixed, it must be applied;
translations.idiomatic: Now that the statutory text is fixed, it must actually be applied;

sentences.zh: 用失其平，不異無律。

translations.literal: if application loses its fairness, it is no different from having no statutes.
translations.idiomatic: if application loses its fairness, it is no different from having no law at all.

sentences.zh: 律書精細，文約例廣，疑似相傾，故誤相亂，一乖其綱，枉濫橫起。

translations.literal: The law books are minute, their text spare yet their precedents broad; where doubt and likeness lean against each other, errors tangle together—once the guiding principle is lost, wrongful judgments rise up unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: The law books are minute, their text spare yet their precedents broad; where doubt and likeness lean against each other, errors tangle together—once the guiding principle is lost, wrongful judgments rise up unchecked.

sentences.zh: 法吏無解，旣多謬僻，監司不習，無以相斷，則法書徒明於帙裏，冤魂猶結於獄中。

translations.literal: Law clerks without understanding commit many perverse errors; supervising officials untrained have no means to pass judgment—then the law books shine only within their bindings while wronged souls still knot themselves in the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Law clerks without understanding commit many perverse errors; supervising officials untrained have no means to pass judgment—then the law books shine only within their bindings while wronged souls still knot themselves in the prisons.

sentences.zh: 今府州郡縣千有餘獄，如令一獄歲枉一人，則一年之中，枉死千餘矣。

translations.literal: Today in prefectures, provinces, commanderies, and counties there are more than a thousand prisons; if in each prison one person is wrongly killed per year, then in one year more than a thousand die unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: Today in prefectures, provinces, commanderies, and counties there are more than a thousand prisons; if each prison wrongly kills one person a year, then in a single year more than a thousand die unjustly.

sentences.zh: 冤毒之死，上干和氣，聖明所急，不可不防。

translations.literal: Deaths born of poisonous injustice offend heaven's harmonious qi—a matter Your Sagely Illumination urgently cares about and cannot fail to guard against.
translations.idiomatic: Deaths born of poisonous injustice offend heaven's harmonious qi—a matter Your Sagely Illumination urgently cares about and cannot fail to guard against.

sentences.zh: 致此之由，又非但律吏之咎，列邑之宰，亦亂其經。

translations.literal: The causes leading to this are not solely the fault of law clerks; the magistrates of the various districts also disorder the guiding principles.
translations.idiomatic: The causes leading to this are not solely the fault of law clerks; the magistrates of the various districts also disorder the guiding principles.

sentences.zh: 或以軍勳餘力，或以勞吏暮齒，獷情濁氣，忍并生靈，昏心狠態，吞剝氓物，虐理殘其命，曲文被其罪，冤積之興，復緣斯發。

translations.literal: Some rely on residual military merit, others on long-serving clerks in their twilight years—brutish in feeling, turbid in spirit, they cruelly swallow the living; dark of heart and savage in manner, they devour the common people, torturing principle to destroy lives and twisting texts to cloak guilt—the rise of accumulated injustice springs again from this.
translations.idiomatic: Some rely on residual military merit, others on long-serving clerks in their twilight years—brutish in feeling, turbid in spirit, they cruelly swallow the living; dark of heart and savage in manner, they devour the common people, torturing principle to destroy lives and twisting texts to cloak guilt—the rise of accumulated injustice springs again from this.

sentences.zh: 獄吏雖良，不能爲用。

translations.literal: Though prison clerks be good, they cannot be put to use.
translations.idiomatic: Though prison clerks be good, they cannot be put to use.

sentences.zh: 使于公哭於邊城，孝婦冤於遐外。

translations.literal: It makes Lord Yu weep at the border fortress and the filial wife suffer injustice in distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: It makes Lord Yu weep at the border fortress and the filial wife suffer injustice in distant lands.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲宥之，其已血濺九泉矣。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty may wish to pardon them, their blood has already splashed the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty may wish to pardon them, their blood has already splashed the nine springs.

sentences.zh: 尋古之名流，多有法學。

translations.literal: Searching among the celebrated men of antiquity, many mastered legal studies.
translations.idiomatic: Searching among the celebrated men of antiquity, many mastered legal studies.

sentences.zh: 故釋之、定國，聲光漢臺；

translations.literal: Hence Shizhi and Dingguo, their fame shining on the Han terrace;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Shizhi and Dingguo, their fame shining on the Han terrace;

sentences.zh: 元常、文惠，績映魏閣。

translations.literal: Yuanchang and Wenhui, their achievements reflected in the Wei pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang and Wenhui, their achievements reflected in the Wei pavilion.

sentences.zh: 今之士子，莫肯爲業，縱有習者，世議所輕。

translations.literal: Today's scholars refuse to make it their profession; even those who study it are slighted in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Today's scholars refuse to make it their profession; even those who study it are slighted in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 良由空懃永歲，不逢一朝之賞，積學當年，終爲閭伍所蚩。

translations.literal: Truly because they toil empty years without meeting a single morning's reward, amassing learning for years only to be mocked by their neighborhood in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because they toil empty years without meeting a single morning's reward, amassing learning for years only to be mocked by their neighborhood in the end.

sentences.zh: 將恐此書永墜下走之手矣。

translations.literal: I fear this book will forever fall into the hands of low runners.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this book will forever fall into the hands of low runners.

sentences.zh: 今若弘其爵賞，開其勸慕，課業宦流，班習冑子，拔其精究，使處內局，簡其才良，以居外仕，方岳咸選其能，邑長竝擢其術，則皐繇之謨，指掌可致，杜鄭之業，鬱焉何遠。

translations.literal: Now if we enlarge their ranks and rewards, open paths of encouragement, set examinations for officials in service, extend instruction to imperial scions, select those of penetrating mastery to place in inner bureaus, choose the talented and good to hold outer posts, have regional governors all select for ability and district chiefs together promote for skill—then Gao Yao's counsels could be attained at a gesture, and the achievements of Du and Zheng, how distant could they be?
translations.idiomatic: Now if we enlarge their ranks and rewards, open paths of encouragement, set examinations for officials in service, extend instruction to imperial scions, select those of penetrating mastery to place in inner bureaus, choose the talented and good to hold outer posts, have regional governors all select for ability and district chiefs together promote for skill—then Gao Yao's counsels could be attained at a gesture, and the achievements of Du and Zheng, how distant could they be?

sentences.zh: 然後姦邪無所逃其刑，惡吏不能藏其詐，如身手之相驅，若絃栝之相接矣。

translations.literal: Then the wicked would have nowhere to escape punishment, and evil clerks could not hide their fraud—as hand and body drive each other, as bowstring and frame join together.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wicked would have nowhere to escape punishment, and evil clerks could not hide their fraud—as hand and body drive each other, as bowstring and frame join together.

sentences.zh: 臣以疏短，謬司大理。

translations.literal: Your servant, being shallow and deficient, has wrongly presided over the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, being shallow and deficient, has wrongly presided over the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 陛下發自聖衷，憂矜刑網，御廷奉訓，遠照民瘼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, moved from the sacred heart, grieves for the penal net; at court you receive instruction and cast your light far upon the people's afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, moved from the sacred heart, grieves for the penal net; at court you receive instruction and cast your light far upon the people's afflictions.

sentences.zh: 臣謹仰述天官，伏奏雲陛。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully sets forth the offices of heaven and submits this memorial prostrate before the cloud steps.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully sets forth the offices of heaven and submits this memorial prostrate before the cloud steps.

sentences.zh: 所奏繆允者，宜寫律上，國學置律助教，依《五經》例，國子生有欲讀者，策試上過高第，卽便擢用，使處法職，以勸士流。

translations.literal: What your servant has memorialized in error yet approved should be inscribed above the statutes; the National University should establish an assistant instructor in law following the precedent of the 《Five Classics》; imperial students who wish to study it should sit for examination and, if they pass with high marks, be immediately promoted to legal posts to encourage the scholar stream.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant has memorialized in error yet approved should be inscribed above the statutes; the National University should establish an assistant instructor in law following the precedent of the 《Five Classics》; imperial students who wish to study it should sit for examination and, if they pass with high marks, be immediately promoted to legal posts to encourage the scholar stream.

sentences.zh: 詔報從納，事竟不施行。

translations.literal: An edict replied that his proposal was accepted, but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that his proposal was accepted, but in the end it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 轉御史中丞，遷驃騎長史，輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor-in-Chief, then promoted to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry General and General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to imperial censor-in-chief, then promoted to chief clerk of the rapid cavalry general and general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 建武初，遷冠軍將軍、平西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West, and Grand Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might, chief clerk of the Pacification of the West, and grand administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 稚珪以虜連歲南侵，征役不息，百姓死傷。

translations.literal: Zhigui, because the barbarians for successive years invaded southward and corvée labor never ceased, with the common people dying and wounded,
translations.idiomatic: Because the barbarians had invaded the south year after year, corvée labor never ceased, and the common people were dying and wounded, Zhigui

sentences.zh: 乃上表曰：

translations.literal: submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 匈奴爲患，自古而然，雖三代智勇，兩漢權奇，筭略之要，二塗而已。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu have been a scourge since antiquity; though the Three Dynasties had wisdom and courage and the Two Han had resourceful stratagems, the essentials of calculation and planning are only two paths.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu have been a scourge since antiquity; though the Three Dynasties had wisdom and courage and the Two Han had resourceful stratagems, the essentials of calculation and planning are only two paths.

sentences.zh: 一則鐵馬風馳，奮威沙漠；

translations.literal: One is iron horses racing with the wind, exerting might in the desert;
translations.idiomatic: One is iron horses racing with the wind, exerting might in the desert;

sentences.zh: 二則輕車出使，通驛虜庭。

translations.literal: the other is light carriages sent on embassy, opening post roads to the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: the other is light carriages sent on embassy, opening post roads to the barbarian court.

sentences.zh: 搉而言之，優劣可睹。

translations.literal: Weighing them together, their relative merit is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing them together, their relative merit is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 今之議者，咸以丈夫之氣，恥居物下，況我天威，寧可先屈？

translations.literal: Those who debate today all take manly spirit and shrink from standing beneath others; how much more under our heavenly majesty—could we bow first?
translations.idiomatic: Those who debate today all invoke manly spirit and shrink from standing beneath others; how much more under our heavenly majesty—could we yield first?

sentences.zh: 吳、楚勁猛，帶甲百萬，截彼鯨鯢，何往不碎？

translations.literal: Wu and Chu are fierce and strong, with a million armored men—cut down those whales and krakens, where would they not be shattered?
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu are fierce and strong, with a million armored men—cut down those whales and krakens, where would they not be shattered?

sentences.zh: 請和示弱，非國計也。

translations.literal: To sue for peace and show weakness is no state policy.
translations.idiomatic: To sue for peace and show weakness is no state policy.

sentences.zh: 臣以爲戎狄獸性，本非人倫，鴟鳴狼踞，不足喜怒，蜂目蠆尾，何關美惡。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the Rong and Di have the nature of beasts and fundamentally belong outside human relations—the owl's cry and wolf's crouch are not worth joy or anger; wasp eyes and scorpion tails have nothing to do with beauty or ugliness.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the Rong and Di have the nature of beasts and fundamentally belong outside human relations—the owl's cry and wolf's crouch are not worth joy or anger; wasp eyes and scorpion tails have nothing to do with beauty or ugliness.

sentences.zh: 唯宜勝之以深權，制之以遠，弘之以大度，處之以蟊賊。

translations.literal: One should only overcome them with deep strategy, control them from afar, magnify them with great forbearance, and treat them as grain-devouring pests.
translations.idiomatic: One should only overcome them with deep strategy, control them from afar, magnify them with great forbearance, and treat them as grain-devouring pests.

sentences.zh: 豈足肆天下之忿，捐蒼生之命，發雷電之怒，爭蟲鳥之氣。

translations.literal: How could one unleash the world's wrath, cast away the lives of the black-haired people, loose thunder-and-lightning anger, and contend over the spirit of insects and birds?
translations.idiomatic: How could one unleash the world's wrath, cast away the lives of the black-haired people, loose thunder-and-lightning anger, and contend over the spirit of insects and birds?

sentences.zh: 百戰百勝，不足稱雄，橫尸千里，無益上國。

translations.literal: A hundred battles, a hundred victories—insufficient to be called heroic; corpses strewn for a thousand li—of no benefit to the superior state.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred battles, a hundred victories—insufficient to be called heroic; corpses strewn for a thousand li—of no benefit to the superior state.

sentences.zh: 而蟻聚蠶攢，窮誅不盡，馬足毛羣，難與競逐。

translations.literal: Yet they gather like ants and swarm like silkworms; pursued to the end they cannot be exterminated—a flock at every horse's hoof, hard to race against.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they gather like ants and swarm like silkworms; pursued to the end they cannot be exterminated—a flock at every horse's hoof, hard to race against.

sentences.zh: 漢高橫威海表，窘迫長圍；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han swept might across the sea's margin yet was pressed hard in prolonged siege;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han swept might across the sea's margin yet was pressed hard in prolonged siege;

sentences.zh: 孝文國富刑清，事屈陵辱；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen made the state rich and punishments clear, yet affairs bent to insult and humiliation;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen made the state rich and punishments clear, yet affairs bent to insult and humiliation;

sentences.zh: 宣帝撫納安靜，朔馬不驚；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuandi soothed and accepted them into quiet, and the northern horses were not startled;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuandi soothed and accepted them into quiet, and the northern horses were not startled;

sentences.zh: 光武卑辭厚禮，寒山無靄。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu used humble words and generous gifts, and the cold mountains knew no mist.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu used humble words and generous gifts, and the cold mountains knew no mist.

sentences.zh: 是兩京四主，英濟中區，輸寶貨以結和，遣宗女以通好，長轡遠馭，子孫是賴。

translations.literal: These two capitals and four sovereigns brilliantly aided the central realm, sending treasure to seal peace and dispatching imperial daughters to open friendship—reins held far, descendants thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: These two capitals and four sovereigns brilliantly aided the central realm, sending treasure to seal peace and dispatching imperial daughters to open friendship—reins held far, descendants thereby secured.

sentences.zh: 豈不欲戰，惜民命也。

translations.literal: Was it that they did not wish to fight? They cherished the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Was it that they did not wish to fight? They cherished the people's lives.

sentences.zh: 唯漢武藉五世之資，承六合之富，驕心奢志，大事匈奴。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Wu of Han, relying on five generations' accumulation and inheriting the wealth of the six directions, with proud heart and extravagant will, made the Xiongnu his great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Wu of Han, relying on five generations' accumulation and inheriting the wealth of the six directions, with proud heart and extravagant will, made the Xiongnu his great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 遂連兵積歲，轉戰千里，長驅瀚海，飲馬龍城，雖斬獲名王，屠走凶羯，而漢之卒甲十亡其九。

translations.literal: Thereupon he linked armies year after year, battled across a thousand li, drove far into the Han Sea, watered horses at Dragon City—though he beheaded famous kings and slaughtered fleeing fierce Jie, nine-tenths of Han's soldiers and armor perished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he linked armies year after year, battled across a thousand li, drove far into the Han Sea, watered horses at Dragon City—though he beheaded famous kings and slaughtered fleeing fierce Jie, nine-tenths of Han's soldiers and armor perished.

sentences.zh: 故衞霍出關，千隊不反，貳師入漠，百旅頓降，李廣敗於前鋒，李陵沒於後陣，其餘奔北，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Hence when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes, a thousand companies did not return; when the Second Division entered the desert, a hundred hosts collapsed in surrender; Li Guang was defeated at the vanguard, Li Ling lost at the rear—the rest fled north in numbers beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Hence when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes, a thousand companies did not return; when the Second Division entered the desert, a hundred hosts collapsed in surrender; Li Guang was defeated at the vanguard, Li Ling lost at the rear—the rest fled north in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 遂使國儲空懸，戶口減半，好戰之功，其利安在？

translations.literal: Thus state stores hung empty and registered households were halved—where lay the profit in loving war?
translations.idiomatic: Thus state stores hung empty and registered households were halved—where lay the profit in loving war?

sentences.zh: 戰不及和，相去何若？

translations.literal: How does war compare with peace—how far apart are they?
translations.idiomatic: How does war compare with peace—how far apart are they?

sentences.zh: 自西朝不綱，東晉遷鼎，羣胡沸亂，羌狄交橫，荊棘攢於陵廟，豺虎咆於宮闈，山淵反覆，黔首塗地，逼迫崩騰，開闢未有。

translations.literal: From the time the Western dynasty lost its guiding rope and Eastern Jin moved the tripod, the many Hu boiled in chaos and Qiang and Di crossed paths—thorns piled at imperial tombs, jackals and tigers roared in palace gates, mountains and abysses overturned, the black-haired people smeared the ground, pressed to collapse and turmoil such as since the world's opening had never been seen.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the Western dynasty lost its guiding rope and Eastern Jin moved the tripod, the many Hu boiled in chaos and Qiang and Di crossed paths—thorns piled at imperial tombs, jackals and tigers roared in palace gates, mountains and abysses overturned, the black-haired people smeared the ground, pressed to collapse and turmoil such as since the world's opening had never been seen.

sentences.zh: 是時得失，略不稍陳。

translations.literal: The gains and losses of that time I shall not set forth even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: The gains and losses of that time I shall not set forth even briefly.

sentences.zh: 近至元嘉，多年無事，末路不量，復挑彊敵。

translations.literal: Coming down to the Yuanjia era, many years passed without incident, yet at the end they failed to measure their strength and again provoked a powerful foe.
translations.idiomatic: Coming down to the Yuanjia era, many years passed without incident, yet at the end they failed to measure their strength and again provoked a powerful foe.

sentences.zh: 遂迺連城覆徙，虜馬飲江，青、徐之際，草木爲人耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon linked cities were overturned and populations uprooted; barbarian horses drank at the Yangtze; between Qing and Xu, every tree and blade of grass seemed a man.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon linked cities were overturned and populations uprooted; barbarian horses drank at the Yangtze; between Qing and Xu, every tree and blade of grass seemed a man.

sentences.zh: 建元之初，胡塵犯塞，永明之始，復結通和，十餘年間，邊候且息。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, Hu dust violated the frontier; at the start of Yongming, communication and peace were renewed—for more than ten years the border beacons rested somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan, Hu dust violated the frontier; at the start of Yongming, communication and peace were renewed—for more than ten years the border beacons rested somewhat.

sentences.zh: 陛下張天造曆，駕日登皇，聲雷宇宙，勢壓河岳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty spreads heaven's creation and calendar, mounts the sun to ascend the throne—your fame thunders through the cosmos, your power presses down on rivers and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty spreads heaven's creation and calendar, mounts the sun to ascend the throne—your fame thunders through the cosmos, your power presses down on rivers and mountains.

sentences.zh: 而封豕殘魂，未屠劔首，長蛇餘喘，偷窺外甸，烽亭不靜，五載於斯。

translations.literal: Yet the sealed boar's lingering soul has not been beheaded by the sword; the long serpent's remaining breath steals glances at outer districts—the beacon towers have not been quiet for five years now.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sealed boar's lingering soul has not been beheaded by the sword; the long serpent's remaining breath steals glances at outer districts—the beacon towers have not been quiet for five years now.

sentences.zh: 昔歲蟻壞，瘻食樊、漢，今茲蟲毒，浸淫未已。

translations.literal: Last year ants undermined the dikes and fistulas devoured Fan and Han; this year insect poison spreads and has not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Last year ants undermined the dikes and fistulas devoured Fan and Han; this year insect poison spreads and has not yet ceased.

sentences.zh: 興師十萬，日費千金，五歲之費，寧可貲計。

translations.literal: To raise an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand gold pieces a day; five years' expense—can it be reckoned in coin?
translations.idiomatic: To raise an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand gold pieces a day; five years' expense—can it be reckoned in coin?

sentences.zh: 陛下何惜匹馬之驛，百金之賂，數行之詔，誘此凶頑，使河塞息肩，關境全命，蓄甲養民，以觀彼弊。

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty begrudge a relay of a single horse, a bribe of a hundred gold, an edict of a few lines—to entice these fierce and stubborn ones, let the Yellow River frontier rest its shoulders, preserve lives at the passes, store armor and nourish the people, and watch their decline?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty begrudge a relay of a single horse, a bribe of a hundred gold, an edict of a few lines—to entice these fierce and stubborn ones, let the Yellow River frontier rest its shoulders, preserve lives at the passes, store armor and nourish the people, and watch their decline?

sentences.zh: 我策若行，則爲不世之福；

translations.literal: If my plan is followed, it will be a blessing unmatched in the age;
translations.idiomatic: If my plan is followed, it will be a blessing unmatched in the age;

sentences.zh: 若不從命，不過如戰失一隊耳。

translations.literal: if it is not followed, the loss is no more than losing one company in battle.
translations.idiomatic: if it is not followed, the loss is no more than losing one company in battle.

sentences.zh: 或云「遣使不受，則爲辱命」。

translations.literal: Some say, "If an envoy is sent and not received, it is a disgrace to the mission."
translations.idiomatic: Some say, "If an envoy is sent and not received, it is a disgrace to the mission."

sentences.zh: 夫以天下爲量者，不計細恥，以四海爲任者，寧顧小節。

translations.literal: One who takes the empire as his measure does not reckon small shame; one who takes the four seas as his charge would rather not cling to minor points.
translations.idiomatic: One who takes the empire as his measure does not reckon small shame; one who takes the four seas as his charge would rather not cling to minor points.

sentences.zh: 一城之沒，尚不足惜；

translations.literal: The fall of one city is still not worth regretting;
translations.idiomatic: The fall of one city is still not worth regretting;

sentences.zh: 一使不反，曾何取慚？

translations.literal: one envoy who does not return—what shame is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: one envoy who does not return—what shame is there in that?

sentences.zh: 且我以權取貴，得我略行，何嫌其恥？

translations.literal: Moreover, if by stratagem we gain advantage and our plan advances even slightly, why shrink from the shame?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if by stratagem we gain advantage and our plan advances even slightly, why shrink from the shame?

sentences.zh: 所謂尺蠖之屈，以求伸也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by the inchworm's bend in order to stretch forward.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by the inchworm's bend in order to stretch forward.

sentences.zh: 臣不言遣使必得和，自有可和之理；

translations.literal: Your servant does not say that sending envoys must secure peace—there is simply a rationale by which peace is possible;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not say that sending envoys must secure peace—there is simply a rationale by which peace is possible;

sentences.zh: 猶如欲戰不必勝，而有可勝之機耳。

translations.literal: just as wishing to fight does not guarantee victory, yet there may be an opportunity for victory.
translations.idiomatic: just as wishing to fight does not guarantee victory, yet there may be an opportunity for victory.

sentences.zh: 今宜早發大軍，廣張兵勢，徵犀甲於岷峨，命樓船於浦海。

translations.literal: Now we should early dispatch a great army and broadly display military might, levy rhinoceros armor from Min and Emei, and order tower ships from the sea's shore.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should early dispatch a great army and broadly display military might, levy rhinoceros armor from Min and Emei, and order tower ships from the sea's shore.

sentences.zh: 使自青徂豫，候騎星羅，沿江入漢，雲陣萬里。

translations.literal: Send them from Qing to Yu, scout horsemen star-clustered, along the river into Han—a cloud of formations for ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Send them from Qing to Yu, scout horsemen star-clustered, along the river into Han—a cloud of formations for ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 據險要以奪其魂，斷糧道以折其膽，多設疑兵，使精悉而計亂，固列金湯，使神茹而慮屈。

translations.literal: Hold strategic passes to seize their spirit, cut grain routes to break their courage, set many decoy forces to make their keen scouts know too much and their plans fall into chaos, firmly array golden ramparts so their gods shrink and their counsels bend.
translations.idiomatic: Hold strategic passes to seize their spirit, cut grain routes to break their courage, set many decoy forces to make their keen scouts know too much and their plans fall into chaos, firmly array golden ramparts so their gods shrink and their counsels bend.

sentences.zh: 然後發衷詔，馳輕驛，辯辭重幣，陳列吉凶。

translations.literal: Then issue a heartfelt edict, dispatch swift relays, eloquent words and heavy gifts, and set forth fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Then issue a heartfelt edict, dispatch swift relays, eloquent words and heavy gifts, and set forth fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 北虜頑而愛奇，貪而好貨，畏我之威，喜我之賂，畏威喜賂，願和必矣。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians are stubborn yet love the unusual, greedy yet fond of goods—they fear our might and delight in our bribes; fearing might and delighting in bribes, they will surely wish for peace.
translations.idiomatic: The northern barbarians are stubborn yet love the unusual, greedy yet fond of goods—they fear our might and delight in our bribes; fearing might and delighting in bribes, they will surely wish for peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下用臣之啟，行臣之計，何憂玉門之下，而無款塞之胡哉？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty employs your servant's proposal and carries out your servant's plan, why worry that below Jade Gate there would be no Hu come in sincerity at the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty employs your servant's proposal and carries out your servant's plan, why worry that below Jade Gate there would be no Hu come in sincerity at the frontier?

sentences.zh: 彼之言戰旣慇懃，臣之言和亦慊闊。

translations.literal: Their words for war are already earnest; your servant's words for peace are likewise full and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Their words for war are already earnest; your servant's words for peace are likewise full and broad.

sentences.zh: 伏願察兩塗之利害，檢二事之多少，聖照玄省，灼然可斷。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that Your Majesty examine the benefit and harm of the two paths and weigh the greater and lesser of the two affairs—by sage illumination and mysterious scrutiny, the decision may clearly be made.
translations.idiomatic: I bow and wish that Your Majesty examine the benefit and harm of the two paths and weigh the greater and lesser of the two affairs—by sage illumination and mysterious scrutiny, the decision may clearly be made.

sentences.zh: 所表謬奏，希下之朝省，使同博議。

translations.literal: This memorial, though mistaken in its presentation, I hope may be sent down to the court ministries for broad deliberation together.
translations.idiomatic: This memorial, though mistaken in its presentation, I hope may be sent down to the court ministries for broad deliberation together.

sentences.zh: 臣謬荷殊恩，奉佐侯岳，敢肆瞽直，伏奏千里。

translations.literal: Your servant wrongly bears extraordinary grace, assisting a frontier prince—I dare unleash blind forthrightness and submit this memorial from a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wrongly bears extraordinary grace, assisting a frontier prince—I dare unleash blind forthrightness and submit this memorial from a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 徵侍中，不行，留本任。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant but did not go, remaining in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as palace attendant but did not go, remaining in his original post.

sentences.zh: 稚珪風韻清疏，好文詠，飲酒七八斗。

translations.literal: Zhigui's bearing and charm were clear and spare; he loved literary composition and song, and could drink seven or eight dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigui's bearing and charm were clear and spare; he loved literary composition and song, and could drink seven or eight dou of wine.

sentences.zh: 與外兄張融情趣相得，又與琅邪王思遠、廬江何點、點弟胤竝款交。

translations.literal: With his cousin by marriage Zhang Rong he matched in temperament and taste; he also had warm friendships with Wang Siyuan of Langye, He Dian of Lujiang, and Dian's younger brother Yin.
translations.idiomatic: With his cousin by marriage Zhang Rong he matched in temperament and taste; he also had warm friendships with Wang Siyuan of Langye, He Dian of Lujiang, and Dian's younger brother Yin.

sentences.zh: 不樂世務，居宅盛營山水，憑机獨酌，傍無雜事。

translations.literal: He took no joy in worldly affairs; his residence lavishly arranged mountains and waters—leaning on his armrest he drank alone, with nothing else beside him.
translations.idiomatic: He took no joy in worldly affairs; his residence lavishly arranged mountains and waters—leaning on his armrest he drank alone, with nothing else beside him.

sentences.zh: 門庭之內，草萊不剪，中有蛙鳴，或問之曰：「欲爲陳蕃乎？

translations.literal: Within his gates and courtyard the grass was not cut; frogs croaked within, and someone asked him: "Do you wish to be like Chen Fan?
translations.idiomatic: Within his gates and courtyard the grass was not cut; frogs croaked within, and someone asked him: "Do you wish to be like Chen Fan?

sentences.zh: 」稚珪笑曰：「我以此當兩部鼓吹，何必期效仲舉。」

translations.literal: " Zhigui laughed and said: "I take this as music from both orchestras—why must I expect to emulate Zhongju?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhigui laughed and said: "I take this as music from both orchestras—why must I expect to emulate Zhongju?"

sentences.zh: 永元元年，爲都官尚書，遷太子詹事，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he became Minister of Justice for the Capital, was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan he became minister of justice for the capital, was transferred to grand tutor of the heir apparent, and was given the additional post of regular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三年，稚珪疾，東昏屏除，以牀轝走，因此疾甚，遂卒。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhigui fell ill; Emperor Donghun had him expelled and he fled in a carrying litter; because of this his illness grew severe and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhigui fell ill; Emperor Donghun had him expelled and he fled in a carrying litter; because of this his illness grew severe and he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十五。

translations.literal: He was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 劉繪字士章，彭城人，太常悛弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Hui, style name Shizhang, was a native of Pengcheng and younger brother of the Minister of Ceremonies Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, whose style name was Shizhang, came from Pengcheng and was the younger brother of Minister of Ceremonies Jun.

sentences.zh: 父勉，宋末權貴，門多人客，使繪與之共語，應接流暢。

translations.literal: His father Mian, a powerful figure at the end of Song, had many guests at his door; he had Hui converse with them, and his responses were fluent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mian, a powerful figure at the end of Song, had many guests at his door; he had Hui converse with them, and his responses were fluent.

sentences.zh: 勉喜曰：「汝後若束帶立朝，可與賔客言矣。

translations.literal: Mian said with pleasure: "If later you gird yourself and stand at court, you may speak with guests.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said with pleasure: "If later you gird yourself and stand at court, you may speak with guests.

sentences.zh: 」解褐著作郎，太祖太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: " Upon leaving the commoner's garb he became Compiler at the Historian's Office and Acting Aide on the staff of the Founding Emperor as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " Upon entering office he became compiler at the historian's office and acting aide on the staff of the Founding Emperor as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 太祖見而歎曰：「劉公爲不亡也。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor saw him and sighed: "Lord Liu is not dead after all."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor saw him and sighed: "Lord Liu is not dead after all."

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷爲江州，以繪爲左軍主簿。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, became governor of Jiang Province and appointed Hui Recorder of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, took up the governorship of Jiang province, he appointed Hui recorder of the left army.

sentences.zh: 隨鎮江陵，轉鎮西外兵曹參軍，驃騎主簿。

translations.literal: He followed the garrison to Jiangling and was transferred to Military Aide in the External Troops Section of the Pacification of the West, then Recorder on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the garrison to Jiangling, then served as military aide in the external troops section of the Pacification of the West and as recorder on the rapid cavalry general's staff.

sentences.zh: 繪聦警有文義，善隷書，數被賞召，進對華敏，僚吏之中，見遇莫及。

translations.literal: Hui was keen-witted and possessed literary discernment, skilled in clerical script; he was repeatedly summoned for reward, and in audience his responses were brilliant and quick—among the staff none was favored as he was.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was keen-witted and literarily accomplished, skilled in clerical script; repeatedly summoned to court, he answered with brilliant quickness in audience—among the staff none was favored like him.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王詡爲功曹，以吏能自進。

translations.literal: Wang Xu of Langye served as Merit Evaluator and advanced himself through bureaucratic competence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu of Langye served as merit evaluator and advanced himself through bureaucratic competence.

sentences.zh: 嶷謂僚佐曰：「吾雖不能得應嗣陳蕃，然閤下自有二驥也。

translations.literal: Yan said to his staff: "Though I cannot obtain one to answer to Chen Fan, yet within my gate there are two fine steeds.
translations.idiomatic: Yan told his staff: "Though I cannot find a successor to Chen Fan, within my gate there are two fine steeds all the same.

sentences.zh: 」復爲司空記室錄事，轉太子洗馬，大司馬諮議，領錄事。

translations.literal: " He again served as Recorder in the Headquarters of the Minister of Works, was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Adviser to the Grand Marshal, and headed the recording office.
translations.idiomatic: " He later served as headquarters recorder to the minister of works, was transferred to groom of the heir apparent and adviser to the grand marshal, and headed the recording office.

sentences.zh: 時豫章王嶷與文惠太子以年秩不同，物論謂宮、府有疑，繪苦求外出，爲南康相。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, and the Literary and Graceful Heir Apparent differed in age and rank; public opinion held that palace and princely establishment harbored mutual suspicion, and Hui bitterly sought to go out, becoming Chancellor of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, and the Literary and Graceful Heir Apparent differed in age and rank; rumor held that palace and princely establishment were at odds, and Hui pressed hard to leave the capital, becoming chancellor of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 郡事之暇，專意講說。

translations.literal: In the leisure of commandery affairs he devoted himself entirely to lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever commandery duties allowed, he devoted himself entirely to lecturing.

sentences.zh: 上左右陳洪請假南還，問繪在郡何似？

translations.literal: The sovereign's attendant Chen Hong requested leave to return south and was asked how Hui was doing in the commandery?
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's attendant Chen Hong requested leave to return south and was asked how Hui was faring in the commandery?

sentences.zh: 旣而閒之曰：「南康是三州喉舌，應須治幹。

translations.literal: Afterward he mentioned in conversation: "Nankang is the throat and tongue of three provinces; it requires a capable administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he remarked: "Nankang is the throat and tongue of three provinces; it requires a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 豈可以年少講學處之邪？

translations.literal: How can one place there a young man who lectures on learning?"
translations.idiomatic: How can one put a young lecturer in charge there?"

sentences.zh: 」徵還爲安陸王護軍司馬，轉中書郎，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: " He was recalled and made Chief of Staff to the Guards Army of the Prince of Anlu, then transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: " He was recalled and made chief of staff to the guards army of the Prince of Anlu, then transferred to secretariat attendant in charge of edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 敕助國子祭酒何胤撰治禮儀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to assist the National University Rector He Yin in compiling and ordering ritual and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to assist National University rector He Yin in compiling and ordering ritual and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 永明末，京邑人士盛爲文章談義，皆湊竟陵王西邸。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming, capital gentlemen flourished in literary composition and discourses on principle, all gathering at the western residence of the Prince of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming, gentlemen of the capital flourished in literary composition and discourses on principle, all gathering at the western residence of the Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 繪爲後進領袖，機悟多能。

translations.literal: Hui was leader among the younger generation, quick-witted and multitalented.
translations.idiomatic: Hui stood at the head of the younger generation, quick-witted and multitalented.

sentences.zh: 時張融、周顒竝有言工，融音旨緩韻，顒辭致綺捷，繪之言吐，又頓挫有風氣。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Rong and Zhou Yong both excelled in speech: Rong's tones were leisurely in cadence, Yong's phrasing elegant and swift, while Hui's utterance was further marked by rhythmic pauses and spirited bearing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Rong and Zhou Yong both excelled in speech: Rong's tones were leisurely in cadence, Yong's phrasing elegant and swift, while Hui's utterance was further marked by rhythmic pauses and spirited bearing.

sentences.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「劉繪貼宅，別開一門。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Liu Hui adjoins the house and opens a separate gate.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time had a saying: "Liu Hui adjoins the house and opens a separate gate.

sentences.zh: 」言在二家之中也。

translations.literal: " Meaning he stood between the two houses.
translations.idiomatic: " Meaning he stood between the two houses.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響誅後，豫章王嶷欲求葬之，召繪言其事，使爲表。

translations.literal: After the Marquis of Yufu, Zixiang, was executed, the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, wished to have him buried and summoned Hui to speak of the matter, ordering him to compose a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: After the Marquis of Yufu, Zixiang, was executed, the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, wished to have him buried and summoned Hui to discuss it, ordering him to compose a memorial.

sentences.zh: 繪求紙筆，須臾便成。

translations.literal: Hui asked for paper and brush and in a moment it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked for paper and brush and finished it in a moment.

sentences.zh: 嶷惟足八字，云「提攜鞠養，俯見成人」。

translations.literal: Yan added only eight characters, saying, "Raised and nurtured in your arms, I looked up and saw him grown."
translations.idiomatic: Yan added only eight characters: "Raised and nurtured in your arms, I looked up and saw him grown."

sentences.zh: 乃歎曰：「禰衡何以過此。

translations.literal: He then sighed: "How could Mi Heng surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: He then sighed: "How could Mi Heng surpass this?"

sentences.zh: 」後北虜使來，繪以辭辯，敕接虜使。

translations.literal: " Later when northern barbarian envoys came, Hui for his eloquence was ordered to receive the barbarian envoys.
translations.idiomatic: " Later when northern barbarian envoys came, Hui for his eloquence was ordered to receive the barbarian envoys.

sentences.zh: 事畢，當撰《語辭》。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded he was to compile the 《Discourse Records》.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was concluded he was to compile the 《Discourse Records》.

sentences.zh: 繪謂人曰：「無論潤色未易，但得我語亦難矣。」

translations.literal: Hui said to others: "Never mind that polishing is not easy—even to get my wording is difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Hui told others: "Never mind that polishing is not easy—even capturing my wording is difficult."

sentences.zh: 事兄悛恭謹，與人語，呼爲「使君」。

translations.literal: In serving his elder brother Jun he was respectful and careful; in speaking with others he addressed him as "My Lord."
translations.idiomatic: In serving his elder brother Jun he was respectful and careful; in speaking with others he addressed him as "My Lord."

sentences.zh: 隆昌中，悛坐罪將見誅，繪伏闕請代兄死，高宗輔政，救解之。
