translations.literal: During Longchang, Jun was charged with a crime and about to be executed; Hui prostrated himself at the palace gate and asked to die in his brother's place; the High Ancestor, assisting in government, rescued and released him.
translations.idiomatic: During Longchang, Jun was charged with a crime and about to be executed; Hui prostrated himself at the palace gate and asked to die in his brother's place; the High Ancestor, assisting in government, rescued and released him.

sentences.zh: 引爲鎮軍長史，轉黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was brought in as Chief Clerk of the Suppression Army and transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought in as chief clerk of the suppression army and transferred to gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 高宗爲驃騎，以繪爲輔國將軍，諮議，領錄事，典筆翰。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was Rapid Cavalry General, he made Hui General Who Assists the State, Adviser, head of the recording office, and in charge of brush and documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor was rapid cavalry general, he made Hui general who assists the state and adviser, head of the recording office, and in charge of brush and documents.

sentences.zh: 高宗卽位，遷太子中庶子，出爲寧朔將軍、撫軍長史。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, Hui was transferred to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and sent out as Pacification General and Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, Hui was transferred to vice director in the heir apparent's household and sent out as pacification general and chief clerk of the pacification army.

sentences.zh: 安陸王寶晊爲湘州，以繪爲冠軍長史、長沙內史，行湘州事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anlu, Bao Ye, became governor of Xiang Province and appointed Hui Chief Clerk of the Army Who Establishes Might and Interior Governor of Changsha, acting on Xiangzhou affairs, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Anlu, Bao Ye, took up the governorship of Xiang province, he appointed Hui chief clerk of the army who establishes might and interior governor of Changsha, with charge of Xiangzhou affairs, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 寶晊妃，悛女也。

translations.literal: Bao Ye's consort was Jun's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ye's consort was Jun's daughter.

sentences.zh: 寶晊愛其侍婢，繪奪取，具以啟聞，寶晊以爲恨，與繪不協。

translations.literal: Bao Ye loved a serving maid; Hui seized her and fully reported it to the throne; Bao Ye resented this and was at odds with Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ye loved a serving maid; Hui took her away and reported the matter fully to the throne; Bao Ye resented this and fell out with Hui.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪去官。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office.

sentences.zh: 有至性，持喪墓下三年，食麤糲。

translations.literal: He had utmost filial nature, observing mourning at the tomb for three years, eating coarse grain.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he observed mourning at the tomb for three years on coarse food.

sentences.zh: 服闋，爲寧朔將軍、晉安王征北長史、南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Pacification General, Chief Clerk on the Northern Campaign of the Prince of Jin'an, and Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai, acting on South Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became pacification general, chief clerk on the northern campaign of the Prince of Jin'an, and grand administrator of southern Donghai, with charge of South Xuzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 繪雖豪俠，常惡武事，雅善博射，未嘗跨馬。

translations.literal: Though Hui was bold and chivalrous, he always disliked military affairs, was elegantly skilled at gambling archery, and never once mounted a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hui was bold and chivalrous, he always disliked military affairs, was elegantly skilled at target archery for sport, and never once mounted a horse.

sentences.zh: 兄悛之亡，朝議贈平北將軍、雍州刺史，詔書已出，繪請尚書令徐孝嗣改之。

translations.literal: At Jun's death the court deliberated posthumous award of General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yong Province; the edict had already been issued when Hui asked Minister Director Xu Xiaosi to change it.
translations.idiomatic: At Jun's death the court deliberated posthumous award of general who pacifies the north and governor of Yong province; the edict had already been issued when Hui asked minister director Xu Xiaosi to change it.

sentences.zh: 及梁王義師起，朝廷以繪爲持節、督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Liang's righteous army rose, the court appointed Hui Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling district of Yingzhou, and the Sui commandery of Sizhou, General Who Assists the State, concurrent Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang's righteous army rose, the court appointed Hui bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling district of Yingzhou, and the Sui commandery of Sizhou, general who assists the state, concurrent colonel pacifying the barbarians, and governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 固讓不就。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 衆以朝廷昏亂，爲之寒心，繪終不受，東昏改用張欣泰。

translations.literal: The multitude, seeing the court benighted and chaotic, felt cold at heart for him, but Hui in the end did not accept; Emperor Donghun then used Zhang Xintai instead.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone, seeing the court benighted and chaotic, feared for him, but Hui in the end refused; Emperor Donghun then appointed Zhang Xintai instead.

sentences.zh: 繪轉建安王車騎長史，行府國事。

translations.literal: Hui was transferred to Chief Clerk on the staff of the Prince of Jian'an as Cavalry General, acting on the princely establishment's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was transferred to chief clerk on the staff of the Prince of Jian'an as cavalry general, with charge of the princely establishment's affairs.

sentences.zh: 義師圍城，南兖州刺史張稷總城內軍事，與繪情款異常，將謀廢立，閑語累夜。

translations.literal: When the righteous army besieged the city, Zhang Ji, Governor of South Yanzhou, oversaw military affairs within the walls; he and Hui were unusually close in affection and were plotting deposition and enthronement, conversing at leisure night after night.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army besieged the city, Zhang Ji, governor of South Yanzhou, oversaw military affairs within the walls; he and Hui were unusually close and plotted deposition and enthronement, talking through the night on many occasions.

sentences.zh: 東昏殞，城內遣繪及國子博士范雲等送首詣梁王於石頭，轉大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: After Donghun perished, those within the city sent Hui and National University Erudite Fan Yun and others to deliver the head to the Prince of Liang at Stone Fortress; Hui was transferred to Attendant of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After Donghun perished, those within the city sent Hui and National University erudite Fan Yun and others to deliver the head to the Prince of Liang at Stone Fortress; Hui was transferred to attendant of the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zhongxing reign.

sentences.zh: 年四十五。

translations.literal: He was forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 繪撰《能書人名》，自云善飛白，言論之際，頗好矜知。

translations.literal: Hui compiled 《Names of Those Skilled at Writing》 and said himself that he was skilled at feibai script; in discourse he rather loved to show off his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Hui compiled 《Names of Those Skilled at Writing》 and claimed skill in feibai script; in conversation he rather loved to show off what he knew.

sentences.zh: 弟瑱，字士溫。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhen, style name Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhen, whose style name was Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 好文章，飲酒奢逸，不𠫤財物。

translations.literal: He loved literature, drank wine in luxurious excess, and was not stingy with possessions.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature, drank lavishly, and was free-handed with his possessions.

sentences.zh: 滎陽毛惠遠善畫馬，瑱善畫婦人，世竝爲第一。

translations.literal: Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses; Zhen was skilled at painting women—both were ranked first in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang excelled at painting horses; Zhen excelled at painting women—both were ranked first in their day.

sentences.zh: 官至吏部郎。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of attendant of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 先繪卒。

translations.literal: He died before Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Hui.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：刑禮相望，勸戒之道，淺識言治，莫辯後先，故宰世之堤防，御民之羈絆。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Punishment and ritual face each other—the way of admonition and warning. Those of shallow understanding speak of governance yet cannot distinguish what comes first and after; hence the dikes of one who governs the age and the halters that restrain the people.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Punishment and ritual face each other—the way of admonition and warning. Those of shallow understanding speak of governance yet cannot distinguish what comes first and after; hence the dikes of one who governs the age and the halters that restrain the people.

sentences.zh: 端簡爲政，貴在畫一，輕重屢易，手足無從。

translations.literal: Upright and simple in government, what is prized is uniformity; when severity and leniency change repeatedly, hands and feet have nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and simple in government, what is prized is uniformity; when severity and leniency change repeatedly, hands and feet have nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 律令之本，文約旨曠，據典行罰，各用情求。

translations.literal: The root of statutes and ordinances: text spare, purport broad; according to the canon punishments are applied, each case judged by its particular circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The root of statutes and ordinances: text spare, purport broad; according to the canon punishments are applied, each case judged by its particular circumstances.

sentences.zh: 舒慘之意旣殊，寬猛之利亦異，辭有出沒，義生增損。

translations.literal: The intent behind leniency and severity already differs; the benefit of clemency and harshness also varies—phrasing has its appearances and disappearances, and meaning gives rise to additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: The intent behind leniency and severity already differs; the benefit of clemency and harshness also varies—phrasing has its appearances and disappearances, and meaning gives rise to additions and subtractions.

sentences.zh: 舊尹之事，政非一途，後主所是，卽爲成用。

translations.literal: Matters of former magistrates follow no single path; what a later ruler approves immediately becomes established practice.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of former magistrates follow no single path; what a later ruler approves immediately becomes established practice.

sentences.zh: 張弛代積，稍至遷訛。

translations.literal: Tightening and loosening accumulate generation by generation, gradually leading to drift and error.
translations.idiomatic: Tightening and loosening accumulate generation by generation, gradually leading to drift and error.

sentences.zh: 故刑開二門，法有兩路，刀筆之態深，舞弄之風起。

translations.literal: Hence punishment opens two gates and law has two paths; the manner of brush and knife runs deep, and the wind of manipulation rises.
translations.idiomatic: Hence punishment opens two gates and law has two paths; the manner of brush and knife runs deep, and the wind of manipulation rises.

sentences.zh: 承喜怒之機隙，挾千金之奸利，剪韭復生，寧失有罪，抱木牢戶，未必非冤。

translations.literal: Seizing the opportune gaps of joy and anger, clutching thousand-gold bribes of wicked profit—cut leeks and they grow again; better to let the guilty go than to clasp wood at the prison gate when the accused may not be wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the opportune gaps of joy and anger, clutching thousand-gold bribes of wicked profit—cut leeks and they grow again; better to let the guilty go than to clasp wood at the prison gate when the accused may not be wronged.

sentences.zh: 下吏上司，文簿從事，辯聲察色，莫用衿府，申枉理讞，急不在躬，案法隨科，幸無咎悔。

translations.literal: Lower clerks and higher superiors, documents and records in hand, judge by voice and scrutinize expression, none employing the breast of judgment; to plead injustice and reason out legal disputes is urgent yet not in one's own person—follow the statute by category and hope for no blame or regret.
translations.idiomatic: Lower clerks and higher superiors, documents and records in hand, judge by voice and scrutinize expression, none employing the breast of judgment; to plead injustice and reason out legal disputes is urgent yet not in one's own person—follow the statute by category and hope for no blame or regret.

sentences.zh: 至於郡縣親民，百務萌始，以情矜過，曾不待獄，以律定罪，無細非諐。

translations.literal: As for commanderies and counties close to the people, where the hundred affairs first sprout—showing mercy for faults by feeling, sometimes without even awaiting trial; fixing guilt by statute, no detail not an offense.
translations.idiomatic: As for commanderies and counties close to the people, where the hundred affairs first sprout—showing mercy for faults by feeling, sometimes without even awaiting trial; fixing guilt by statute, no detail not an offense.

sentences.zh: 蓋由網密憲煩，文理相背。

translations.literal: This is because the net is dense, the statutes burdensome, and text and principle oppose each other.
translations.idiomatic: This is because the net is dense, the statutes burdensome, and text and principle oppose each other.

sentences.zh: 夫懲恥難窮，盜賊長有，欲求猛勝，事在或然，掃墓高門，爲利孰遠。

translations.literal: For shame in punishment is hard to exhaust and thieves and bandits ever exist; to seek triumph through harshness is a matter of mere chance—sweeping tombs and lofty gates, which profit is farther off.
translations.idiomatic: For shame in punishment is hard to exhaust and thieves and bandits ever exist; to seek triumph through harshness is a matter of mere chance—sweeping tombs and lofty gates, which profit is farther off.

sentences.zh: 故永明定律，多用優寬，治物不患仁心，見累於弘厚，爲令貴在必行，而惡其舛雜也。

translations.literal: Therefore the statutes of Yongming largely used leniency and breadth; in governing things one need not fear a benevolent heart, though one may be encumbered by expansive generosity—what is prized in ordinances is that they must be carried out, while what is hated is their confusion and mixture.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the statutes of Yongming largely used leniency and breadth; in governing things one need not fear a benevolent heart, though one may be encumbered by expansive generosity—what is prized in ordinances is that they must be carried out, while what is hated is their confusion and mixture.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：袁徇厥戚，猶子爲情。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yuan followed his kin, treating a nephew's bond as kinship.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Yuan followed his kin, treating a nephew's bond as kinship.

sentences.zh: 稚珪夷遠，奏諫罷兵。

translations.literal: Zhigui dwelt aloof and distant, memorializing to remonstrate and halt the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigui dwelt aloof and distant, memorializing to remonstrate and halt the armies.

sentences.zh: 士章機悟，立行砥名。

translations.literal: Shizhang was quick-witted and perceptive, establishing conduct that whet his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhang was quick-witted and perceptive, establishing conduct that sharpened his reputation.

translations.literal: Footnote marker [1].
translations.idiomatic: Footnote 1.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Southern Qi》, January 1972.
